summary.title: A/B testing mistakes I learned the hard way
summary.one_liner: Eight common A/B testing pitfalls, from including unaffected users to over-relying on metrics, and how to avoid each one.
keywords: how to avoid a/b test errors
why do a/b test results mislead
takeaways: Filter out ineligible users before they enter an experiment, so results are not diluted.
Break results down by subgroups (device, tenure, channel, etc.) to catch Simpson's paradox.
Predetermine experiment duration and check statistical power to avoid the peeking problem.
Run a small test rollout (e.g., 5%) to verify logging, crash rates and group ratios before full launch.
Monitor counter metrics and consider holdout tests; write clear hypotheses and remember A/B tests are not the only decision input.
summary.summary: The author, a former growth engineer at Meta who has run hundreds of A/B tests, lists eight classic experimentation mistakes with examples. Each section explains the problem, such as including unaffected users, viewing only aggregate results, or stopping early, and gives a practical fix. Fixes include filtering eligible users in code, segmenting results by subgroup, setting a duration with a running-time calculator, staged rollouts, monitoring counter metrics, accounting for seasonality, and writing specific hypotheses. The post is written by PostHog staff and ends with a note that metrics are not the only reason to ship a change.
